title: Agency awards Harbour Systems a $412 million contract for autonomous patrol vessels
text:
Agency awards Harbour Systems a $412 million contract for autonomous patrol vessels

The Example Defence Agency today announced a contract valued at $412 million with Harbour Systems, a privately held maker of uncrewed surface vessels, to deliver 38 autonomous patrol boats over 36 months.

Under the award, Harbour Systems will build the vessels at its two existing yards and stand up a third assembly line. The first 6 boats are due within 12 months of contract signature. The agency said the programme includes an option for a further 20 vessels, which is not funded under today's award.

"This contract moves autonomous patrol from trials to a fielded fleet," the agency's programme director said in the announcement.

Harbour Systems said it expects to add about 450 jobs across its yards. The company did not disclose the unit price, its margin on the work, or how much of the award is tied to delivery milestones.

The agency noted that the award followed an open competition with 4 bidders and remains subject to the standard protest period of 10 days, during which an unsuccessful bidder may challenge the decision. Deliveries depend on the supply of marine batteries, which the agency described as constrained.

Harbour Systems is privately owned and has no publicly traded shares.
